transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-10
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Patel (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Ironbridge - Head of Compliance), Ethan Shaw (Ironbridge - Platform), Priya Nair (Ironbridge - Product), Samir Gupta (Ironbridge - Procurement)

Summary (auto): Brief discovery focused on data residency controls, evidence for audits (SOC2/HIPAA), log retention constraints for regulated trading data, and feasibility of region-locking requests to EU-only or on-prem nodes. Agreed next steps: share SOC2/HIPAA docs, diagram EU-only deployment, schedule benchmark with sample data.

Topics: data residency, audit evidence, logging retention & redaction, KMS/HSM key control, VPC/private control plane, dedicated vs hosted trade-offs, timeline for pilot/POC.

Transcript:
00:00 Avery (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick round-robin — I'll kick it off, I'm Avery, AE on the Redwood side, and Diego is our solutions engineer.
00:07 Marta (Ironbridge): Hi, Marta here — head of compliance for Ironbridge. We have Ethan, our platform engineer, Priya from product, and Samir from procurement.
00:12 Diego (Redwood SE): Nice to meet you all. High-level — we understand Ironbridge is looking at a mix of hosted and private for inference; today we'd like to understand constraints so we can map to Hosted / Dedicated / Private options.
00:20 Ethan (Ironbridge): Right. Two big constraints for us: 1) Regulatory rules around trade-related PII and audit logs — some of that must remain in the EU, and 2) We have strict log retention policies, and in some cases logs can't include full request payloads.
00:30 Priya (Ironbridge): Also timeline — we'd like to evaluate options for a pilot in May, with production decisions by end of Q2.
00:37 Avery: Great. Marta, can you walk us through the compliance evidence you need? SOC2? HIPAA? Financial controls?
00:42 Marta: SOC 2 is table stakes. For certain feeds we also need to show traceability for any model inference that touches regulated accounts — that means an audit trail, per-request metadata, and a way to demonstrate region residency. For some data fields we need to ensure they are never logged in raw form.
00:56 Diego: Understood. On the Redwood side we support a few things — hosted API with region routing, Dedicated with reserved capacity in a region, and Private (VPC / on-prem) where control plane is isolated. We also have KMS integrations for customer-managed keys and HSM options.
01:10 Marta: The tricky part — our auditors ask for proof that no raw payloads left the EU for certain customers, and that logs with sensitive fields were redacted at point of ingestion. How do you demonstrate that?
01:20 Diego: We can do a few layers. First, region-locking: requests can be routed and pinned to a region — that means inference and ephemeral KV caches remain in the selected region. Second, we can enable field-level redaction at the proxy side and only keep hashed/aggregated traces in logs. Third, for evidence, we can provide architecture diagrams, system logs showing host IPs in-region, and attestation docs (SOC2/HIPAA).
01:39 Marta: When you say "region-locking," is that a guarantee or a configuration? We need a contractual guarantee that EU-data stays in EU for the customers in scope.
01:45 Avery: For Hosted we provide region preference and routing policies — but a contract-level guarantee typically requires Dedicated or Private where you can commit to regional isolation and controls. We can propose a Dedicated pool physically provisioned in the EU with contractual language for residency.
01:58 Samir (Ironbridge): So hosted won't meet legal guarantee? That will impact pricing and procurement if we need Dedicated or Private.
02:05 Avery: Correct — Hosted is strong for many customers, but Dedicated or Private is the path for formal residency SLAs. We can map pricing and timelines.
02:12 Ethan: About logs — we must ensure request payloads with account identifiers never end up in long-term logs. Is there a way to have ephemeral debugging logs kept short-lived and scrubbed, and only aggregated metrics preserved?
02:22 Diego: Yes. We have a configurable retention pipeline. By default, we retain structured request metadata (latency, model version, token counts) and index fields that are non-PII. Raw request bodies can be disabled or routed to ephemeral storage that auto-deletes within X hours. For ironbridge use-case we can set that to zero retention and send a redaction policy at the proxy layer.
02:40 Marta: Can you do field-level redaction reliably? We have some nested payloads, trading notes, and sometimes account numbers are embedded in free text.
02:48 Diego: We have two options: pre-ingest scrubbing at the SDK/proxy where you define patterns to strip, and post-ingest redaction where the runtime scrubs tokens via a deterministic redaction policy. For high compliance customers we recommend pre-ingest scrubbing plus customer-side encryption.
03:05 Priya: On customer-side encryption — do you support customer-managed keys? If we hold keys in our KMS, does Redwood ever have access to plaintext?
03:12 Avery: We support KMS integrations and an HSM-backed option in Dedicated/Private. If you supply the key material and we only hold wrapped keys, we can configure zero-access so Redwood does not have plaintext access. We'll share the KMS integration guide.
03:24 Ethan: That sounds like a Private deployment then. How invasive is the Private install? We have strict network segmentation and SRE constraints.
03:31 Diego: Private can be deployed into your VPC, and we provide a private control plane with a lightweight agent. There is an on-prem bundle if needed; some customers run the inference worker nodes in their network and maintain control of EBS volumes and disk encryption.
03:45 Marta: For audit evidence, what artifacts do you provide? We need logs that show model version, requestid, timestamp, and host region. For HIPAA we need encryption at rest/in transit attestations and an incident response playbook.
03:57 Avery: We'll provide SOC 2 type II report, HIPAA BAAs where applicable, encryption diagrams, and a security playbook. We also can provide per-request logs with redaction demonstrated in a test.
04:10 Ethan: One more — some of our trading flows require sub-30ms latency. Dedicated in-region helps, but we also need to understand batching and caching behavior — K V cache persistence could be considered state and might be subject to retention policies. How do you handle KV cache eviction and residency?
04:25 Diego: Good question. KV cache is ephemeral and treated as transient memory in the runtime. For Dedicated and Private we can guarantee it never hits durable storage and lives on the GPU/instance memory. For Hosted, we may persist small checkpoints for warm-start which we can disable for your account.
04:40 Marta: We will need documentation stating KV is ephemeral and not persisted to a cross-region store.
04:45 Avery: Noted — Diego will add that to the architecture doc.
04:48 Priya: Regarding logs stored for incident response — what's the shortest retention you can commit to? Some regulators want 7 years for audit trails, but for raw payloads we need minimal retention.
05:00 Diego: We can set raw payload retention to 0 days (disabled) and keep structured audit metadata for longer windows. For your use-case we suggest raw disabled, structured logs retained 90 days by default but configurable; we can discuss longer archival for audit-only data in an isolated store with stricter access controls.
05:18 Marta: For some EU clients, we have a policy: raw inference payloads must be purged within 24 hours and be EU-only. Would Redwood be able to demonstrate a purge?
05:27 Diego: Mechanically yes — we can show deletion events and storage back-end logs, and in Dedicated/Private you control the deletion trigger. For Hosted we'd need a contractual SLA.
05:36 Samir: Pricing question — does Dedicated EU pool have a lead time and a premium? We're trying to budget.
05:42 Avery: Typical lead time to provision a Dedicated pool in EU is 4–6 weeks depending on capacity; pricing is a reserved monthly commit. We can produce a ballpark today and firm numbers after we size with Diego.
05:55 Ethan: Security scanning and pen testing — will you provide a redacted pentest report? We can't give full internal freetext to vendors.
06:02 Diego: We can provide redacted pentest summaries and a set of mitigations. Also we can run joint tests in a staging environment with your team if you require it.
06:10 Priya: A question on multi-tenant vs single-tenant models — if we choose Dedicated, is each customer's traffic logically separated?
06:17 Diego: In Dedicated, you get reserved capacity: often single-tenant for your workloads or a small tenancy pool dedicated to your account. For strongest guarantees, Private (VPC/on-prem) is single-tenant in your network.
06:26 Marta: Another auditor ask — can you show a chain of custody for keys used to encrypt logs? Who has access?
06:32 Avery: We can show KMS role mappings and IAM policies. With customer-managed KMS, you control access. Diego will note which IAM roles are involved and we can export a sample access audit.
06:41 Ethan: For the benchmarking — we want to see per-token cost estimates when we force EU-only routing and disable caching, because caching helps cost but may be disallowed for some regulated calls.
06:51 Diego: We can model cost for three profiles: aggressive caching (default), caching disabled for protected routes, and a hybrid with prefix caching only. We'll include latency/throughput delta.
07:02 Priya: Can Redwood redact PII fields at inference time so that the model never sees them? For example, token placeholders replace account numbers before hitting the model.
07:11 Diego: You can do client-side tokenization and replacement, or we can implement a pre-processing hook in the proxy that replaces matched patterns with placeholders. That requires rule maintenance but is doable.
07:22 Marta: Are there any compliance gaps you know of for financial services — e.g., requirements you don't meet out of the box?
07:28 Avery: From experience, the common gaps are: 1) Hosted without a residency SLA, 2) Raw payload retention defaults, 3) Lack of customer-managed KMS. All of these are addressable with Dedicated/Private and some configuration work.
07:40 Samir: Procurement will need an SOW and an SLA draft. What level of SOC2/HIPAA evidence will you include in the SOW?
07:47 Avery: We'll include SOC2 Type II, HIPAA BAA language for covered workloads, and residency clauses for Dedicated. We'll attach the redacted pentest and the incident response playbook as exhibits.
07:56 Marta: One last technical — are audit logs tamper-evident? We need a way to show they weren't modified after generation.
08:03 Diego: We can stream logs into an append-only store or provide signed log entries; for Private you can write them directly to your auditing stack. For Hosted/Dedicated we can enable signed audit entries and provide the signing key evidence.
08:14 Ethan: That would satisfy our auditors.
08:16 Avery: Okay, to wrap — Diego and I will share: (1) SOC2/HIPAA attestation & redacted pentest; (2) an EU-only deployment diagram and note on KV cache behavior; (3) a cost model for caching disabled vs enabled; (4) propose bench dates week of 4/20. Marta/Ethan to provide sample data schema and retention rules.
08:30 Priya: We'll prep the sanitized sample dataset.
08:33 Marta: Also, Diego — please include an explicit note that KV cache does not persist to cross-region storage and that you can disable warm-start checkpoints.
08:40 Diego: Will do.
08:42 Samir: From procurement perspective, please include lead times and cancellation terms as well.
08:45 Avery: We'll include a procurement appendix.
08:47 Marta: Any final questions?
08:49 Ethan: No, that's it. Thanks, very helpful.
08:51 Avery: Thanks — we'll send the items over.

Recap & explicit next steps (auto):
- Avery to send SOC2 Type II, HIPAA BAA template, redacted pentest summary, encryption diagrams (due 2026-04-13).
- Diego to prepare EU-only region diagram, explicit KV cache statement, and sample k8s manifest for Private/Dedicated (due 2026-04-16).
- Ironbridge (Ethan) to provide anonymized sample dataset and schema for benchmarking (due 2026-04-17).
- Schedule bench week of 2026-04-20 — Diego to propose slots.

End of transcript.
